Three workers heading home to Monterrey after a maintenance job in Nuevo Laredo were involved in a rollover on Carretera Nacional on Thursday night, and two of them were injured — including the driver, who was taken to an IMSS hospital in serious condition, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The crash happened at about 10 p.m. at kilometer 10 of Carretera Nacional, in the north-to-south lanes, according to the report. Front-seat passenger Vicente told the outlet that a trailer forced their car off the road; the driver lost control, struck the ramp of the lateral road, and the car overturned.

The three men work for Servicios Industriales Especializados del Norte, a Monterrey-area maintenance company, and had been doing maintenance at PepsiCo facilities in Nuevo Laredo, according to El Mañana. The article identifies them only by first name: Javier, the driver; Vicente, the front passenger; and Isai, the rear passenger. Their vehicle was an older-model Ford Ikon with Nuevo León plates.

Javier was the most seriously hurt, striking the steering wheel and suffering several fractured ribs and severe blows to the chest, according to the report. He was described as in very poor health and was taken by Red Cross ambulance to an IMSS hospital for specialized care. Vicente suffered a wound to his right arm. Isai was unharmed — a detail worth noting, since the headline's wording suggested three injuries, while the article's account says two were injured and the third was not.

Protección Civil personnel found the three men outside the vehicle and examined them, firefighters assessed the scene, Red Cross paramedics treated the occupants, and Vialidad officers took note of the facts, according to the report. No further official findings were given.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Volcadura deja tres trabajadores heridos en la Carretera Nacional," October 30, 2026
